newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane steady to higher, good demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane steady to higher, good demand.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices were steady to higher in late trade on Tuesday, in line with firmer NYMEX crude oil futures and strong demand in the Midwest, players said.
In Conway, Kansas, hub propane traded at a day high of 47.00 cents a gallon, after opening up to hungry buyers who immediately bought parcels at 45.75 cents.
Traders said farm cooperatives and major customers, such as producers, were both in the market Tuesday for barrels.
"When you get that combination out in the market on the same day, prices are going to go up," said one Conway trader.
Cool, wet weather that rolled into the Midwest early Tuesday brought out farmers in need of propane to use as fuel to dry their corn crops.
Dealings in Mont Belvieu, Texas, however were light, although players said propane showed a firmer sentiment given the run-up in NYMEX November crude oil futures.
Propane remained between 48.50 cents and 48.75 cents a gallon, with a deal heard done at 48.75 cents, traders said.
November crude oil futures ended up 70 cents at $24.07 a barrel, helped by concerns of a possible oil-related fallout from reports suggesting Russian President Yeltsin has serious health problems.
-- Laney Salisbury New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
